Its `assets/*.hbs` templates were diffed against packages/create/templates at the pinned SHA: identical (the tarball adds only build-time copies images/, initial-data.json, products.csv). The generated app depends on @vendure/core 3.7.3 etc. from the registry; the generated package-lock.json is not part of upstream, so a snapshot is tracked at campaigns/node/vendure/starter-snapshot/.

packageManager.name: npm
packageManager.install: performed by @vendure/create --ci --use-npm (npm install in the generated app); build: `npm run build:server && npm run build:worker` (tsc via vendure CLI); dashboard not built

buildAdaptations: Dashboard (vite) build skipped; only `vendure build server|worker` (tsc). npm cache on the bind-mounted workspace.
Dependencies: `npm uninstall better-sqlite3 && npm install --save-exact pg` (pg 8.23.1), as the create template does for postgres.
configAdaptations: SQLite -> PostgreSQL (root decision, round 2): src/vendure-config.ts dbConnectionOptions changed to exactly what the pinned create template (templates/vendure-config.hbs) renders for `--db postgres` (type 'postgres', database/schema/host/port/username/password from DB_NAME/DB_SCHEMA/DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD); src/environment.d.ts gains the matching DB_* declarations. sha256 of vendure-config.ts 61af4d02... -> 765f8c96...; no other source file changed.

The create tool's own postgres path starts a docker-compose database on the host and cannot run in the build container, so seeding replicates its CI populate step (harness/seed-populate.cjs = create-vendure-app.ts populate with synchronize:true, initial-data.json and products.csv from the pinned tarball's assets) against a throwaway PostgreSQL, then pg_dump (seed.sql, sha256 97006d4d82b6a08fb3a603261fd06a47a8fbe0fa8ab2d034e488414f3074e0c0) is restored into a fresh database for every baseline.
The in-process job-queue entry from round 1 is REMOVED; the stock two-process topology is used.

Env: PORT=3000, APP_ENV=dev, DB_*, DO_NOT_TRACK=1, VENDURE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1; superadmin credentials are the create tool's published CI defaults (synthetic, local only); the server port is published to 127.0.0.1 only.

knownLimits: Per ADR 0005 / root decision: GraphQL operations are not enumerated; this harness sends GraphQL only because that is how Vendure's HTTP API is spoken. Operation names in scenarios.mjs are harness-internal labels and are never meant to be recovered by X-trace.

SQLite is no longer used; round-1 evidence: with SQLite the stock two-process topology failed with `SqliteError: database is locked` in Vendure 3.7.3, which is why PostgreSQL was adopted by root decision. Round-1 baselines (baseline-1..3, SQLite, in-process queue) are retained privately and superseded.
Dashboard UI, asset uploads, GraphiQL, scheduler tasks not exercised. Upstream test suites not run.

instrumented.status: NOT RUN (preparation only). Documented for the later packaged-candidate run.
instrumented.xtraceVersionAtPreparation: slice/v001-node-capture 09aba20 provides only the node:http server request root (adapters/node/packages/adapter-core/src/http-capture.cts); Express/Nest/Fastify framework modules and DB-driver seams required by ADR 0005 are not present on that branch, so only the HTTP-root assertions below are currently satisfiable; the framework/DB rows become required as those modules land.
procedure: 1. node harness/run.mjs prepare|create+build (once) -> immutable pinned workspace.

2. Start PostgreSQL (restore the seed) fresh exactly as in the baseline (harness reset), then launch the app with the packaged `xtrace` as the process launcher inside the same linux/arm64 Docker image (or on the host with the same Node major) instead of plain `node`.
3. Run the same scenarios (same harness code, same request bodies); compare each scenario's semanticEffectFingerprint with baseline-<n>/scenarios.json; any difference fails the scenario.

4. Query X-trace (CLI/API/browser) for the recording of each request and assert handler/intermediate/DB/outcome rows listed in `scenarios[].expectedSeams`, with wrong-association checks for `concurrent-writes-and-reads` (every recording holds only its own route params, response and DB statements).

5. Stop/restart X-trace, reopen persisted captures in the packaged browser; privacy canaries (synthetic secrets in request bodies, headers, cookies, DB values) must not appear in wire/logs/storage/API/exports/diagnostics; measure overhead (baseline vs instrumented p50/p95 and throughput over repeated runs).
instrumented.launcher: Two traced processes: `xtrace run -- node ./dist/index.js` (server) and `xtrace run -- node ./dist/index-worker.js` (worker), cwd app, same DB_* env; npm scripts start:server/start:worker or `vendure start all` are launcher-propagation variants.

seamsByLayer.httpRoot: node:http server created by Nest platform-express (required)
seamsByLayer.express: Express 5.2.1 under Nest: route POST /shop-api and POST /admin-api (apollo middleware), GET /health, /assets
seamsByLayer.nest: Nest provider-method frames only: controller methods and @Resolver() class methods executed through Nest's external context creator (ADR 0005 root decision 3: no reviewed_internal GraphQL hook; ordinary application method frames from probes on application code); guards/pipes/interceptors where safely observable
seamsByLayer.intermediateApplicationCall: Vendure service methods (ProductService.create/update/softDelete/findOne, OrderService.addItemToOrder/adjustOrderLine, AuthService) in @vendure/core dist/service/services/*.js
seamsByLayer.db: TypeORM -> pg Client.query (SQL text sanitized, binds excluded); worker process issues its own pg statements on job_record/search_index_item
seamsByLayer.outcome: HTTP status; GraphQL errors/ErrorResult are HTTP 200 and must be reported honestly as handler-level outcomes only where observable without GraphQL enumeration
seamsByLayer.negativeAssertion: no GraphQL document, operation name, variable or schema introspection on the wire, in storage/API/UI/exports (ADR 0005 negative test); POST /shop-api and POST /admin-api appear as exactly two endpoints with many recordings; the UI says 'GraphQL operations are not enumerated'
seamsByLayer.worker: job_record INSERT in the server recording and the separate worker process's job execution; linkage via the job id/db row is an X-trace design question, report honestly if unlinked

ledger.receiptShape: tools/release/check_ledger.py (slice/v001-control-admission) validate_receipt/_validate_special: schemaVersion 1; requirementId; result 'passed'; candidateSha == exact candidate; build{id,sourceSha,artifactSetSha256} bound to the accepted logical release build; artifacts[] {path,sha256} (packaged xtrace artifacts in the accepted set); evidence[] {path,sha256}; checks[] each {status:'passed', reached:true}; kind 'campaign'; attestation{upstream{canonicalUrl (https), sha (40-hex), stableTag}, scenarios[>=5]{name, baseline{path,sha256}, instrumented{path,sha256}, browser{path,sha256}, privacy{path,sha256}, overhead{path,sha256}, semanticEffectFingerprint (64-hex) == instrumentedSemanticEffectFingerprint}, artifacts[]}; signatures[] containing a trusted 'campaign-runner' role signature.
ledger.fromThisPreparation: baseline-<n>/scenario-index.json (written by lib/export-scenarios.mjs) supplies, per scenario, name, baseline{path,sha256} and the 64-hex semanticEffectFingerprint; the instrumented run must reproduce each fingerprint exactly and write instrumentedSemanticEffectFingerprint, instrumented/browser/privacy/overhead evidence files. Skipped, unreached or synthetic assertions never count.
